title: delegated-rollback-token-economics-and-approval-heuristics-prd-wip
content:
Overview:

This is a working PRD draft exploring a design for delegated rollback tokens paired with lightweight approval heuristics and compact audit logging for customer-managed networking in Private deployments. The goal is to enable fast, permissioned rollbacks (or emergency rollforwards) that balance safety, auditability, and cost for both small pilot customers and large enterprise tenants.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Private deployments require strict change controls for customer-managed VPC/networking, but strict gates can slow recovery in incidents.
- Operators and SREs want a predictable, minimizable audit footprint for changes while preserving forensic detail when required.
- Enterprise security teams want delegation patterns (e.g. partner-managed operators, customer security ops) to be able to trigger rollbacks without full operator escalations but must retain revocation and billing visibility.

Goals (success criteria):
1) Safety: Rollback actions are authorized and reversible only within defined policies.
2) Audit minimalism: Default logs are compact (token references + hashes) with on-demand forensic expansion.
3) Delegation: Customers can delegate rollback capability to operator roles (human or automation) with scoped TTLs and revocation.
4) Economics: Token issuance/retention has clear cost impact and predictable storage/SLA tradeoffs.
5) UX: Rollback path < 3 clicks for authorized users in Console; API path < 200ms request latency for token validation.

Scope:
- Focus: customer-managed networking changes (VPC peering, route updates, nat/gateway swaps) and lifecycle of rollback tokens tied to change bundles.
- Out of scope: full CI/CD orchestration for application-level rollbacks (this integrates with existing rollout APIs).

High-level proposal (concept):
1) Change Bundle + Rollback Token: When an operator or automated change is created, Redwood issues a compact, signed rollback token representing the change-bundle-id, scope, and policy constraints (expiration, max-rollbacks).
2) Delegated Issuance: Tokens can be created by primary operators or delegated principals (customer-admins, partner agents) depending on policy. Delegation is expressed in a small ACL catalog attached to customer account metadata.
3) Token Economics: Tokens are lightweight (approx 1 KB metadata + 256-bit signature). Storage model: short-lived tokens stored with compact index for 90 days by default, long-term forensic snapshots only retained on explicit request or under enterprise-retention contracts.
4) Approval Heuristics: A set of configurable heuristics decide when a human approval is required to issue or use a rollback token vs. when automated delegated use is allowed. Heuristics include change-risk-score, customer tier, time-of-day, and previous-change-frequency.
5) Compact audit paths: The default audit log records token-ids, principal, timestamp, change-bundle-hash, and a pointer to an encrypted forensic blob (not expanded unless requested).

Design details:

Change bundle model:
- Each operational change creates a change-bundle object (CBID) containing: list of resource diffs, providing system, initiator, requested window, and an optional pre/post snapshot hash.
- CBIDs are immutable and content-addressed; their full blobs can be stored off-line (e.g. encrypted S3 in customer's KMS) or in compact form depending on retention policy.

Rollback token schema (minimal):
- token_id: UUID
- cbid: change-bundle-id (content hash)
- issued_by: principal id
- delegated_from: optional principal id (if delegated)
- scope: list of resource selectors (e.g. subnet-*, route-table-123)
- controls: {expires_at, max_uses, require_2fa, require_manual_approval_on_use}
- signature: platform-signed HSM-backed signature

Approval heuristics (examples and policy presets):
- Preset: low-risk (minor tag-only changes): token issuance allowed automatically for delegated principals with TTL 24h and max_uses 1. Minimal log retained for 30 days.
- Preset: medium-risk (gateway replacements): require two independent operator approvals OR delegated principal with 2FA, token TTL 12h. Expanded forensic snapshot retained 90 days.
- Preset: high-risk (broad route changes, tenant-isolation-affecting): require manual canary rollback plan + senior approval; token issuance only to primary operator.
- Heuristic inputs: resource-change-surface-area, historical rollback rate for resource, time since last host-level change, customer SLA tier, active incident flag.

Delegation model and revocation:
- Delegation catalog: customer-admins may create delegation entries (principal, allowed-scopes, TTL defaults, max-rollbacks) stored as a compact ACL.
- Revocation: immediate revocation via invalidation list (blacklist) and by bumping a delegation-version index. Token use checks real-time revocation index.
- Emergency escalation: a higher-level emergency token can be minted by SREs that overrides some heuristics but is recorded as high-severity event and requires post-facto audit expansion.

Audit storage and minimalism:
- Default audit record (compact): {timestamp, token_id, cbid, principal, action, result, digest_pointer} ~ 200B per event.
- Forensic blob: encrypted full diff of change-bundle and snapshots; stored only when change exceeds preset risk or when requested via support/legal hold.
- Expansion workflow: Support/Legal/Customer can request expansion; expansion entails decrypting forensic blob (requires KMS key or enterprise escrow) and appending to event. This action itself is logged as high-sensitivity.

Token economics (estimates and levers):
- Unit costs (estimates): compact audit record stored in warm index ~ $0.002 per record per month (indexing & query amortized). Forensic blob retention (S3 + KMS + retrieval) ~ $0.15 per MB-month.
- Typical change bundle sizes: small (1–5 diff items, 0.1–0.5 MB forensic), medium (5–30 diffs, 0.5–5 MB), large (>30 diffs, >5 MB).
- Cost controls: default retention window can be reduced for non-enterprise customers; customers can opt into pay-for-retention for longer forensic windows.
- Billing surface: token issuance is non-billable; forensic retention beyond default free window is billable as add-on (separate line item).

Operational UX (Console + API):
- Console flow for issuing a token: create change → preview bundle → choose delegation/principal → system shows suggested preset (auto/manual) → issue token (one-click if allowed).
- Console flow for using a token (rollback): select CBID → present token (auto via Console) → system performs preflight checks (scope, revocation, concurrent locks) → execute rollback.
- API: POST /private/v1/changes -> returns cbid + possible token issuance URL. POST /private/v1/tokens/{id}/use -> validates signature + policy + revocation. Responses include compact event references for audit.

Telemetry, SLOs and alerts:
- SLOs: token validation latency 95th < 200ms; token issuance 95th < 500ms.
- Ops alerts: sudden spike in rollback token uses (> x / hour per customer), failed token validations > threshold, forensic-expansion requests from legal.
- Observability: per-customer histograms of token issuance, average change size, average number of rollbacks per CBID.

Security considerations:
- Tokens signed by HSM-backed key; tokens include nonce to mitigate replay.
- KMS integration for forensic blobs; customer KMS preferred for enterprise to avoid cross-tenant exposure.
- Token exposure mitigation: tokens are bearer artifacts; console masks tokens and APIs require authenticated principals. Add optional 2FA binding for high-risk tokens.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Default retention window: 30 vs 90 days—tradeoff between forensic readiness and cost/attack surface.
- Delegation UX: how fine-grained should scope selectors be? (resource-level vs pattern-level).
- Revocation propagation latency: acceptable window for stale revocations in distributed caches.
- Billing model acceptance: will customers accept add-on forensic retention billing? Need pilot conversations.

Proposed next steps / milestones:
- 2-week spike: implement token schema + local validation library (ENG-serving-runtime & infra) -> prototype. (JIRA: JIRA-PRV-789)
- 4-week UX: Console flows + policy presets + admin delegation UI (DX & product). (GH PR prototype linked above)
- 6-week pilot: onboard 2 customers (one mid-market, one enterprise) to test heuristics and retention economics. Collect per-change telemetry and revise cost model.
- Legal/Compliance review: finalize forensic expansion and data retention contract language.

Action items (owners):
- Maya (product): schedule pilot outreach, finalize heuristics matrix draft.
- Priya (security): draft key-pair lifecycle and token-signing policy; small threat model.
- Liam (infra): prototype token validation lib + revocation index design.
- Diego (finance): model economics for warehouse and forensic retention pricing tiers.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally a lightweight, exploratory draft. We're aiming for a pragmatic approach that keeps the default footprint small while offering enterprise-grade forensic capabilities behind opt-ins and contract language. Feedback wanted on delegation UX, default retention, and the set of heuristic signals we should support out of the gate.

References and examples:
- Similar pattern: short-lived OAuth refresh tokens + revocation lists (analogy).
- Pilot telemetry interest: track mean time to rollback (MTTR), number of manual approvals per rollback, and per-customer cost delta for forensic retention.

End of draft.
